The study will address the student demographics’ unique challenges by 
attempting to unveil ways to optimise the e-learning experience, and better 
cater to GCSE students’ unique needs and preferences. 
The following questions were designed to address significant gaps within existing 
research related to e-learning technologies. The Chosen questions aim to answer 
problems related to student engagement, motivation, content mastery and 
recollection when compared to a core-features-only e-learning application. 
1. How does the use of spaced repetition affect user retention in GCSE 
students? 
2. How does short-form content interleaved with questions affect the 
attention span, engagement and content understanding of GCSE 
students? 
3. To what extent do competitive leader boards, digital badges and 
achievements motivate students? 
The proposed hypothesis is: “The integration of short-form content with 
questions, spaced repetition, digital badges, and competitive leader boards will 
significantly enhance student engagement, retention, and academic 
performance.” 
To validate the hypothesis, a mixed method research approach must be 
employed; this will utilise user engagement metrics, academic performance, 
quantitative data analysis along with qualitative feedback from students and 
teachers.
